A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OptimalThinkingBench by the same authors. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 33 models, efficiency methods, routing and prompting, plus quantitative analyses and qualitative cases.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds math-subset results, a math-versus-general comparison and an additional prompting condition.

M1.justification: The constrained generation/filtering pipeline and evaluated reward-shaping, merging and routing procedures are retained. Added datasets, evaluation rules and prompting comparisons do not establish a revision to a proposed model or algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds MATH Level 1–2 problems as OvT-Math and AIME’25/HMMT’25 competition problems as UT-Math, substantially extending the benchmark's problem-solving coverage. The original general-query domains and 11 Reasoning Gym tasks remain; geometry and logic were already present in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: V2 Table 9 adds an evaluated 'Only Answer' prompting comparator for three Qwen3 models. The original 33-model roster, five efficiency methods and trained/oracle routers remain after matching renamed entries and appendix relocations.

E3.justification: V2 introduces math-verify scoring for the added math subsets and explicitly macro-averages UnderthinkingBench accuracy across reasoning and math. The reported general-query sample count changes from 1440 to 1327, alongside 133 easy-math and 60 competition-math questions. Underthinking token reporting is also revised from 'thinking tokens' to complete output tokens, without establishing whether the implementation changed.

E4.justification: V2 Figure 3 adds a four-model diagnostic comparing accuracy, token use and adjusted accuracy between math and general questions. Table 9 extends prompt sensitivity analysis with 'Only Answer'. Existing domain, answer-type, distractor, model-size and five qualitative-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify eight evaluation seeds and 128 responses per model for selecting qualitative cases. The significance-colored answer-type comparison, Spearman analyses and existing error-bar reporting remain unchanged; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: The expanded benchmark produces extensively revised leaderboard and intervention results: reported overall scores change from 72.7 to 71.1 for o3 and from 62.5 to 68.3 for GPT-OSS-120B. These are different-coverage results, not demonstrated same-setting performance changes. V1 Table 2 survives as v2's non-math Table 7, while new combined-benchmark and 'Only Answer' results are added.

T1.justification: The filtering condition, OAA definition, normalized area-under-curve equation, harmonic-mean score and stated mathematical properties are retained. V2 adds no theorem, proof or substantive derivation; the new subset aggregation concerns evaluation protocol.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden the benchmark description to include easy and competition-level math. The introduction qualifies its regeneration claim to the benchmark's synthetic components. The central contributions and claim that evaluated models fail to balance efficiency and accuracy remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations about limited transfer of efficiency across math and general tasks and more explicitly attributes computation allocation to superficial cues. It removes v1's paragraph interpreting distillation as harming simple-query accuracy. Existing overthinking/underthinking failure explanations largely persist.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly documents extracting the last boxed answer with a regular expression and falling back to the response without its reasoning trace. V2 also identifies math-verify and explains complete-output token reporting. These disclosures do not establish that existing answer-processing procedures changed; the code-access link remains the same.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for MATH, AIME, MathArena and Math-Verify, removes the GPT-4o and o3/o4-mini system-card references, and explicitly calls the benchmark the first unified one. The substantive earlier related-work discussion is largely retained in Appendix A.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites and condenses the introduction and results narrative, combines experimental setup and results under Experiments, and moves Related Work after the analyses. Detailed setup, related work and analyses are redistributed across reorganized appendices.

P2.justification: V2 adds the three-panel math/general Figure 3, replaces the full main leaderboard with a representative-model table plus appendix detail, and summarizes routing and prompting tables across models. Generation diagrams and the distractor plot move to appendices, while detailed tables and case-study pagination are reorganized.

improvement.justification: Expanded math coverage and clearer answer-processing details offer benefits over v1, but the new math-domain analysis contains unresolved numerical reporting. V2 Figure 3 gives o3 accuracy 0.996, 335 tokens and AUCOAA 0.084 on OvT-Math. If token usage is the reported mean, Equation 1 with tmax=1000 implies AUCOAA at least 0.661. The PDF does not reconcile this discrepancy, leaving the reliability of important new evidence—and the net quality improvement—uncertain.
